verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. Same inequality, assumed of strictly fewer coefficients, so the theorem carrying it is stronger. Term by term: `region t` is Ω_{aν}, `t.1` is c_{aν}, `Cc m / Pc m / Kc m` are C_I / P_I / K_I, and `(1 + |Real.log (q x)|)` is Λ_log(q) = 1 + |log q| as fixed on p. 56. Lean indexes the constants by the derivative order m only — not by the term t — which is exactly the paper's 'may be chosen common to that list for each fixed I' and independence of the truncation index. Two encoding points: (i) ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m c‖ bounds all Cartesian multi-indices I of order exactly m simultaneously, where the paper indexes by I ∈ ℕ_0^4; since there are finitely many I of each order the two directions convert by a constant absorbed into C_I resp. Cc m. (ii) Lean quantifies `∀ t ∈ P.terms`, i.e. over ν ≥ 1 only: the field-independent term `P.constant` (= c_{a0}, with Ω_{a0} = Ω in the paper) gets only a smoothness hypothesis and no growth bound at all. That is the paper's own observation that 'The terms c_{a0}, which are independent of U, cancel from that comparison', made into a formal weakening of the hypothesis. The paper's requirement that Ω_{aν} contain the field factors' supports before and after cutoffs is carried separately, by `hrawsupport` and `hcutsupport` (FactorSupportAt off `region t`), not by (5.32) itself.
